hints.text: Both terms are perfect squares, separated by a minus sign.
The pattern $a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)$ applies with $a = x$ and $b = 3$.

learningObjective: Factor a difference of two squares.
explanation: The pattern is $a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)$, giving $(x + 3)(x - 3)$.
Expanding confirms it: $x^2 - 3x + 3x - 9 = x^2 - 9$ ✓. Choice A expands to $x^2 - 6x + 9$, which has a middle term the original does not.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the middle term vanishes
steps: That cancellation is the whole reason the difference of squares factors so cleanly.
It is the single most frequently used factoring pattern on the SAT — recognizing "square minus square" on sight is worth real points.
